summary: Kelani-Peliyagoda Seaplane Base (KEZ) is a water aerodrome situated on the Kelani River in the Peliyagoda area north of central Colombo. It serves as a departure point for domestic seaplane flights, primarily catering to tourists traveling to coastal and resort destinations around Sri Lanka. The base offers a distinctive alternative to conventional airports, allowing passengers to board float-equipped aircraft directly from the river.
faqs:
Q: What type of aircraft operate from Kelani-Peliyagoda?
A: The base primarily serves small float-equipped aircraft, typically twin-engine turboprops used for short domestic routes across Sri Lanka.

Q: Where can I fly to from this seaplane base?
A: Seaplane services from Peliyagoda generally connect Colombo with popular coastal and resort destinations such as the southern beaches, the east coast, and cultural heritage sites around the island.

Q: How early should I arrive before my seaplane flight?
A: Passengers are typically advised to arrive at least 30-60 minutes before scheduled departure to complete check-in and boarding procedures on the floating dock.

Q: Is the seaplane base accessible to tourists?
A: Yes, it is accessible to both domestic and international travelers, though most passengers are tourists booking scenic or point-to-point transfers rather than scheduled public transport.
transport_tips: The seaplane base is located in Peliyagoda, roughly 8-10 km north of Colombo Fort, and is best reached by taxi or private car as public transport options nearby are limited. Traffic in the Colombo metropolitan area can be heavy, so allow extra time during morning and evening rush hours. Some seaplane operators offer complimentary transfers from major Colombo hotels, which is worth checking when booking.
local_tip: Request a seat on the right side of the aircraft if possible — on many southern routes from Colombo, this side typically offers better views of the coastline and Indian Ocean during the descent.
